questions.question: What does alcohol do to your driving skills and judgment?

options.text: It helps driving skills but harms your judgment.
It harms both driving skills and judgment.
It has no effect on either driving skills or judgment.
It has no effect on judgment but harms driving skills.

questions.correctAnswerText: It harms both driving skills and judgment.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time and makes it hard to see clearly. It also affects your judgment about speed and distance, makes you take more risks, and lowers your inhibitions.

questions.question: What causes "highway hypnosis"?

options.text: Staring at the roadway for long periods of time.
Taking frequent rest stops.
Getting too much sleep the night before.
Taking short trips on expressways.

questions.correctAnswerText: Staring at the roadway for long periods of time.
questions.explanation: Highway hypnosis happens when you stare straight ahead and stop looking around your vehicle. You zone out and may not notice traffic slowing down or stopping in front of you.

questions.question: When should you always use your turn signal?

options.text: When changing lanes.
When pulling into or out of a parking space.
When pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Always use your turn signal when changing lanes, pulling into or out of a parking space, or pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area. Signals warn other drivers and help prevent accidents.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Right turn.
T intersection ahead.
Lane change.
Road curve.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a T intersection is coming up ahead.

questions.question: What happens when drivers eat or drink while driving?

options.text: They make no driving errors.
They have trouble driving slowly.
They are better drivers because they are not hungry.
They have trouble controlling their vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They have trouble controlling their vehicles.
questions.explanation: Eating, drinking, or smoking while driving is dangerous. These activities take your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road. Drivers who do these things have trouble staying in their lanes and controlling their vehicles.

questions.question: How should a seat belt be adjusted?

options.text: It should be loose.
It should be buckled snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
It should be hidden beneath the seat.
It should stop the seat belt buzzer or light from working.

questions.correctAnswerText: It should be buckled snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
questions.explanation: The lap belt should fit snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen. The shoulder belt should sit comfortably so you can fit your fist between the belt and your chest.

questions.question: What should you do when changing lanes?

options.text: Signal your intention before changing lanes.
Check your blind spot.
Make sure the lane is clear before entering.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Always signal for enough time before changing lanes or exiting a freeway. Turn your head and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before moving left or right.

questions.question: When should you always use your signal?

options.text: When changing lanes.
When pulling into or out of a parking space.
When pulling into traffic from a parking area or alley.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Always use your turn signal when moving left or right. Use your signal when pulling into traffic from a parking space, moving into a new lane, or passing another vehicle.

questions.question: When must you stop at a railroad crossing?

options.text: When directed to do so by a flagger.
When it is controlled by a stop sign.
When flashing red signals and gates are present and operating.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger directs you to stop, when a stop sign controls it, or when flashing red signals and gates are operating.

questions.question: What problems do worn or bald tires cause?

options.text: They make turning more difficult.
They are likely to hydroplane.
They increase your stopping distance.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Worn or bald tires increase your stopping distance and make turning more difficult. Tires without enough tread also increase the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is approaching.
Look both ways as you cross the intersection.
Always come to a full stop at the intersection.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: Slow down as you approach a yield sign. Be ready to stop and let other vehicles and pedestrians go first. You must stop if traffic requires it.

questions.question: When driving on an interstate:

options.text: Stop on the shoulder if you are tired.
You should always use cruise control.
Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.
You should change lanes often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Always signal, check your mirrors, and check your blind spot before changing lanes or passing. Only stop on the shoulder in emergencies. Avoid cruise control in heavy traffic or bad weather.

questions.question: Traffic signs and pavement markings:

options.text: Must always be obeyed.
Are merely suggestions.
Must be followed only when there is other traffic.
Must be followed only when a police officer is present.

questions.explanation: Traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings control traffic flow and guide drivers safely. You must always obey them.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Low clearance.
Fines double in a work zone.
No left turn.
Do not block intersection.

questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells drivers that the road ahead has low clearance for tall vehicles.

questions.question: The best way to reduce your risk of injury or death in a crash is to:

options.text: Wear your seat belt.
Limit your driving to weekdays.
Stay in the right lane on multilane highways.
Limit your driving to 3:00 p.m. to 6:00 p.m.

questions.explanation: Wearing your seat belt is the single most effective way to protect yourself from death or injury in a crash.

questions.question: Anything that requires you to ____ could cause you to crash.

options.text: Take your eyes off the road
Take your hands off the wheel
Take your attention away from driving
All of the above

questions.explanation: A distraction is anything that takes your attention away from driving, takes your eyes off the road, or takes your hands off the wheel.

questions.question: A steady green light at an intersection means that you:

options.text: Must slow down and prepare to stop.
Must stop and check for oncoming traffic before proceeding.
May drive through the intersection if the road is clear.
May not turn right.

questions.correctAnswerText: May drive through the intersection if the road is clear.
questions.explanation: A steady green light means you may drive through if the road is clear. You may turn right or left unless a sign says no. Always yield to other vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection.

questions.question: Before starting the engine, you should:

options.text: Be sure only backseat passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Be sure only adult passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Be sure only child passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Be sure all passengers have buckled their seat belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be sure all passengers have buckled their seat belts.
questions.explanation: Develop a routine before driving. Buckle your own seat belt and make sure all passengers buckle theirs before starting the engine.

questions.question: If your turn signals fail, you should use ____ to show that you are turning.

options.text: Your horn
Your headlights
Hand signals
Your emergency flashers

questions.explanation: Use hand signals to show when you are turning if your turn signals do not work.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Pedestrians walking along the road ahead.
Pedestrian crossing ahead.
Pedestrians must not cross here.
Be alert for construction workers on the road.

questions.explanation: This sign warns that a pedestrian crossing is ahead. Drive carefully and watch for people crossing the road.

questions.question: If your car breaks down on a highway, what should you do?

options.text: Stay in your car and wait for help.
Turn on your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.
Honk your horn at passing cars.
Flash your headlights at oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.
questions.explanation: If your car breaks down on the highway, turn on your hazard flashers right away. Move your car as far off the road as possible. Raise your hood so other drivers know your car is disabled.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Cars in the right lane must slow down.
No left turn.
Merge.
Pass only in the right lane.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that two lanes of traffic are about to become one lane. You need to merge safely.

questions.question: When you approach railroad tracks, what should you do?

options.text: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
Speed up to cross before the gate closes.
Try to drive around a lowered gate.
Ignore how many tracks you need to cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: When you see railroad tracks, look both ways, listen for trains, slow down, and be ready to stop. A train or other vehicle may be using the tracks.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, what should you do?

options.text: Stop immediately.
Help injured people.
Call the police.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle right away. If possible, move it out of traffic. Call the police and ask for an ambulance if someone is hurt. Help stop any bad bleeding, but do not move injured people unless necessary. Wait for help to arrive.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop.
Wrong way.
Yield.
Do not enter.

questions.explanation: This triangular sign means "Yield." Slow down and check for traffic. Let pedestrians and other vehicles go first. Stop only if you need to.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver who arrives first.
The driver who arrives last.
One driver should go without stopping.
One driver should wave others ahead.

questions.explanation: All four drivers must stop at a four-way stop. The driver who arrives first goes first. If two drivers arrive at the same time, the driver on the right goes first.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must turn left or right.
You are at a T intersection.
Your road is crossing a divided highway.
You are driving over a divided highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your road is crossing a divided highway.
questions.explanation: This sign means your road crosses a divided highway. A divided highway has two separate one-way roads with a median or barrier between them.

questions.question: How can you prevent hydroplaning?

options.text: Keep your tires in good condition with deep tread.
Keep your tires filled to the right pressure.
Drive slower when it rains.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: To prevent hydroplaning, check that your tires have good tread and are filled to the correct pressure. Slow down when driving in rain. Hydroplaning happens more often at higher speeds.

questions.question: Drinking alcohol and driving is:

options.text: A small traffic safety problem.
A serious traffic safety problem.
Safe if you only have a few drinks.
Dangerous only to the person drinking.

questions.explanation: Driving while drunk is a serious safety problem. You cannot drive safely after drinking alcohol or using drugs. It puts you and everyone else on the road in danger.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road curves right ahead. Slow to the safe speed shown.
A divided highway is starting. Slow to the safe speed shown.
Merge ahead. Slow to the safe speed shown.
Winding road ahead. Slow to the safe speed shown.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves right ahead. Slow to the safe speed shown.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that the road curves to the right. Slow down to the safe speed shown on the sign (35 mph in this case).
